newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Bomb kills one in eastern Nigerian oil city.
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills one in eastern Nigerian oil city.

text.p: A bomb in Nigeria's southeastern oil city of Port Harcourt killed a 12-year-old boy and wounded his two companions, newspapers reported on Thursday.

"An explosive device concealed in a tin wrapped in a polythene bag was detonated by one of the boys who picked it up as it was thrown from a moving vehicle," the independent Guardian newspaper said. Other papers carried similar reports.

Military-ruled Nigeria has been hit by a spate of bomb blasts since last year, most of which have targeted soldiers. The last one, in May, killed two people at a mosque in the eastern city of Onitsha.
Newspapers said local police were unwilling to say the blast had been caused by a bomb, but that bomb disposal experts had been sent to the scene.
Twelve opposition activists including exiled Nobel prize laureate Wole Soyinka have been charged with treason in a Lagos magistrates court over the bombings.
The umbrella opposition group the National Democratic Coalition, which is accused by the police of involvement, has denied having anything to do with the attacks.
Port Harcourt is the principal base for oil companies operating in southeastern Nigeria. The West African country pumps more than two million barrels of crude oil every day.
